info.title: ThreatBridge
info.description: The HTTP API of ThreatBridge's map. docs/API.md has the conventions (times, windows, the time range, filters, queries as POST, writes, errors), the filter grammar and what marks mean. Every response here lists every field it has.

delete.summary: Unmark a host, with the marked flows it is an end of

The inside hosts that talked to an address, a network or a domain name (ATK-11)

get.summary: The case's evidence files with their SHA-256 (D31)
get.description: Hashing starts on the first ask and runs in the background; ask again (about once a second) until done. The digests are kept until a file changes. Case backend only.

get.description: Hashing starts with GET /api/evidence; this only estimates it. The map asks before hashing projected to take more than 5 minutes. Case backend only.

get.summary: One hop: who connected to a host, or who it connected to, before or after the anchor
get.description: Who connected to ip (in) or who it connected to (out), in the window before the anchor or after it (time; by default before for in, after for out). Hosts on the exclude list are left out. When the window and the time range don't overlap, start is after end and peers is empty. With filters, counts, times, ports and protocols are those of the flows that pass.

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: the host

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: in (the default): who connected to it; out: who it connected to

parameters.name: time
parameters.description: before or after the anchor; blank: before for in, after for out

parameters.name: ts
parameters.description: the anchor; blank: now

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: per hop: a number and a unit (s, m, h, d, w), at most max_window; default default_window

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: peers to return, 1 to max_limit (larger values are capped); default default_limit

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: top (most connections, the default) or bottom (rarest)

parameters.name: range_from
parameters.description: the start of the analyst's time range: only flows that started in it count

parameters.name: range_to
parameters.description: the end of the analyst's time range

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: a filter expression (D17); repeat for several, combined with AND

post.description: Who connected to ip (in) or who it connected to (out), in the window before the anchor or after it (time; by default before for in, after for out). Hosts on the exclude list are left out. When the window and the time range don't overlap, start is after end and peers is empty. With filters, counts, times, ports and protocols are those of the flows that pass.

parameters.name: dst_time
parameters.description: dst's IOC time: the path reaches dst by then

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: per hop: a number and a unit (s, m, h, d, w), at most max_window; default default_window

parameters.name: hops
parameters.description: the hop limit, 1 to limits.hops; default threat_hops

parameters.description: the start of the analyst's time range: only flows that started in it count

get.summary: Is the service up

post.summary: The marked hosts, and the marked and suspect flows on the drawn connections
post.description: For a CSV export. Without the case backend, the marked flows only.

post.summary: A Security Onion flow's packets, from its sensor through SOC
post.description: The PCAP file, as an attachment, extracted by the sensor that saw the flow, through SOC's Connect API. Needs a SOC API client (TB_SOC_CLIENT_ID, TB_SOC_CLIENT_SECRET; Security Onion Pro), else 501. The request waits for the sensor, up to TB_PCAP_TIMEOUT seconds; a 502 says why the sensor could not provide it, with the SOC job's link where there is one.

mutualTLS.description: the container: a client certificate signed by the ThreatBridge CA

localToken.description: local mode (python -m threatbridge, plain HTTP): the login token it printed at start-up

localCookie.name: tb_token_5055
localCookie.description: local mode: the cookie that opening the printed address sets, named after the port (tb_token_<port>)

write.name: X-ThreatBridge
write.description: required on every write: browsers can't add it to a cross-site request

E400.description: a parameter or the body is invalid; the message says which

E401.description: local mode: the request carries no valid login token (cookie or Authorization: Bearer)

E403.description: a write without the X-ThreatBridge header

E409.description: a map is already saved under that name

E500.description: a shared file (exclude list, marks, saved map) is not valid JSON; it is left for someone to fix

E501.description: this needs another backend (threat lines, paths and suspect connections: the case backend; PCAP downloads: Security Onion with a SOC API client)

E421.description: local mode: the Host header names an address this server doesn't answer to (TB_ALLOWED_HOSTS)

E502.description: Elasticsearch or SOC failed or answered unexpectedly

AccountLabel.description: An account a Windows Security event ties to a flow (D28).

account.description: DOMAIN\user, or user@REALM for Kerberos events

event.description: the event ID that tells it

logon_type.description: 4624: the logon type (3 network, 8 network cleartext, 10 remote)

host.description: the computer the event names: where it was logged, or the service's host

events.description: the event IDs that tell it

AccountsQueryBody.description: The query's parameters as a JSON object (text or numbers), plus filters and marks.

pairs.description: each pair of marked hosts with a path between them

interval.description: the median seconds between the flows' starts

jitter.description: the median absolute deviation of those intervals, as a share of interval

size_jitter.description: the same for the flows' bytes, as a share of their median

score.description: 0 to 1: how regular the intervals and sizes are

start.description: the first flow's start; null for an empty case

end.description: the last flow's start; null for an empty case

dns_names.description: names in the evidence's DNS answers

leases.description: DHCP holdings: who held which address when (D27)

logons.description: flows labelled with the account that made them, from Windows Security events (D28)

Config.description: What a client needs to know about this server (D20).

api_version.description: the API version this server speaks

default_window.description: a query's window when it gives none (TB_WINDOW)

default_limit.description: peers per expansion when a query gives none (TB_LIMIT)

max_limit.description: the most peers per expansion (TB_MAX_LIMIT); larger limits are capped

rare_scan_cap.description: distinct peers the rarest scan looks at (TB_RARE_SCAN_CAP)

soc_pivots.description: whether SOC pivots and PCAP links apply (not for the case backend)

analysis.description: whether threat lines and paths are available (case backend)

suspects.description: whether marks hide what isn't on a line through them (POST /api/suspect; case backend)

marks_poll.description: seconds between the map's checks for other analysts' marks

protocol_names.description: how the map names each protocol: {"ssl": "TLS", "krb": "Kerberos", ...}; others in capitals

live_dns.description: whether domain names on the exclude list are also looked up (TB_LIVE_DNS)

internal_nets.description: the client's own networks: inside hosts (TB_INTERNAL_NETS)

beacon_score.description: the score from which a scored group is a beacon (TB_BEACON_SCORE)

beacon_min.description: the flows a beacon needs at least (TB_BEACON_MIN)

long_connection.description: seconds from which a flow is long (TB_LONG_CONNECTION)

flows.description: its flows with the target, both ways

peers.description: the target's addresses it exchanged flows with

target.description: the target as read: an address, a network, or a domain name

addresses.description: the target's addresses some inside host exchanged flows with; for a domain, from the capture's DNS answers

hosts.description: the inside hosts, earliest first, at most limits.contacts

connections.description: the connections of the first limit hosts, as the map draws them

ports.description: the most used destination ports, up to 5

left.description: seconds still to go at the rate so far; null until it can tell, 0 once done

modified.description: its modification time, now (as built if missing)

protocols.description: the protocol names, as the map shows them; any other Zeek service in capitals works too

MapDocument.description:
A saved map (D19, D22): its hosts where they were, its connections with their counts as drawn,
the highlights (classes), the view, the toolbar, the filters, its own marks and the queries it was
built from, in order. The map reads only what it understands and leaves out what is malformed.

id.description: the flow's id, from its flow list

ports.description: the most used destination ports, up to 5

protocols.description: every protocol the flows carry, sorted: named as Zeek names its services (`dns`, `http`, `smb`, `ssl` for TLS, ...), plus `icmp`, and `unknown` for flows nothing identified. Security Onion gives Zeek's own; case files are identified from the payload, then by well-known port

protocol.description: Zeek's name, as in other answers

start.description: the start of the range counted; null: open

ProtocolsQueryBody.description: The query's parameters as a JSON object (text or numbers), plus filters and marks.

capture.description: addresses in DNS answers in the evidence (pcaps, or Security Onion's DNS records)

anchor.description: the time the map starts from

map.description: as it was saved; the map saves a MapDocument

truncated.description: a direction stopped at limits.threat_line_hosts hosts

ThreatLineQueryBody.description: The query's parameters as a JSON object (text or numbers), plus filters and marks.
